quick: Second-trimester termination: ~150 mL of 0.1% solution instilled extra-amniotically (about 50 mg per 50 mL; total ~150 mg); topical antiseptic 0.1% solution applied to skin/wounds
Used specifically to induce mid-trimester abortion; otherwise not for use in continuing pregnancy
Limited data; systemic exposure from topical use is negligible
No specific data; systemic absorption from topical use is minimal
For induced abortion: uterine activity, bleeding, infection, completeness of expulsion; for topical use: local irritation
summary: Ethacridine lactate is a yellow acridine-derivative antiseptic with broad antibacterial activity used topically for skin and wound disinfection (historically known as Rivanol). It is also widely used in some countries as an intra/extra-amniotic instillation to induce abortion in the second trimester of pregnancy, where instillation into the extra-amniotic space stimulates uterine contractions and expulsion of the fetus over 24-48 hours. It is not approved by the US FDA; evidence and use derive from international/WHO and regional sources.
indications: Topical antiseptic for cleansing and disinfection of skin, wounds, and mucous membranes (0.1% solution)
Induction of second-trimester abortion / intrauterine fetal demise management by extra-amniotic or intra-amniotic instillation (regional use)

dosage.d: Extra-amniotic instillation of 0.1% ethacridine lactate solution, approximately 1.5 mL per estimated week of gestation, commonly a total of about 150 mL (around 150 mg)
dosage.t: Single instillation; may repeat after 24-48 h if no expulsion; often combined with oxytocin
dosage.n: Total dose generally not exceeding ~500 mg; performed under medical supervision

dosage.d: 0.1% (1 mg/mL) aqueous solution applied to the affected area, or as soaked dressing/compress
dosage.t: As needed, one or more times daily

admin: For abortion: instilled into the extra-amniotic (or intra-amniotic) space by a trained clinician using aseptic technique, often followed by oxytocin augmentation
For topical use: apply the 0.1% solution to clean skin or wounds, or as a wet compress; for external use only
Avoid contact with eyes unless using an ophthalmic-appropriate preparation
The solution stains skin and fabrics yellow
moa: As an antiseptic, ethacridine is a cationic acridine dye that binds bacterial DNA and interferes with nucleic acid function, giving bacteriostatic activity mainly against gram-positive organisms. For abortion induction, extra-amniotic instillation acts as a local irritant/stimulant that increases endogenous prostaglandin release and myometrial activity, producing uterine contractions and cervical ripening that lead to expulsion of the products of conception.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to ethacridine or acridine dyes
For abortifacient use: any contraindication to uterine evacuation, suspected uterine rupture, or active genital tract infection
relative: Prior uterine surgery / scarred uterus (caution with induced contractions)
Cardiac or renal disease (for abortifacient procedures)
Application to large open or deep wounds where systemic absorption may rise
monitor: Uterine activity and vaginal bleeding during induced abortion
Signs of infection and completeness of expulsion

preg: Ethacridine for abortion induction is used intentionally to terminate a second-trimester pregnancy under medical supervision. As an antiseptic it is not intended to affect a continuing pregnancy, and systemic absorption from intact-skin topical use is negligible.
lact: There are limited data on ethacridine in breast milk. Systemic exposure from topical antiseptic use is negligible, so it is generally considered compatible with breastfeeding; the abortifacient indication does not apply to lactating women maintaining pregnancy.
renal: No specific renal dosing data are available. Systemic absorption from topical application is minimal; for intrauterine instillation, use with caution in significant renal disease.
hepatic: No specific hepatic dosing data are available. Systemic exposure from topical use is minimal.

major: Oxytocin and prostaglandins - intentionally combined during abortion induction to augment uterine contractions (use under supervision)
minor: No significant systemic drug interactions reported for topical antiseptic use
interactions.diagnostics: Yellow staining of skin/secretions; no characteristic laboratory test interference

common: Yellow staining of skin and dressings
Lower abdominal cramping and bleeding (abortifacient use)
rare: Disseminated intravascular coagulation (rare complication of mid-trimester abortion)
emergency: High fever / signs of sepsis after instillation
Severe abdominal pain or signs of uterine rupture

monitoring: Uterine contractions, bleeding, and vital signs during and after induced abortion
Temperature and signs of intrauterine infection
Local skin reaction for topical use
counsel: For topical use: apply only to the skin; the solution will stain skin and clothing yellow
Do not swallow; keep away from the eyes unless prescribed for that use
If used to end a pregnancy, expect cramping and bleeding over 1-2 days and stay under medical care
Report heavy bleeding, fever, foul discharge, or severe pain after the procedure
Stop and seek advice if a skin rash or irritation develops with topical use
pk: Abortifacient: uterine activity typically begins within hours; expulsion usually within 24-48 hours
Not characterized; systemic levels from topical use are very low
Abortifacient effect develops over 24-48 hours after instillation
Store the solution protected from light; avoid contamination; discard discolored solution
pearls: NOTE: Ethacridine is NOT approved by the US FDA; this record is based on EMA/regional pharmacopoeia, WHO, and published obstetric literature rather than an FDA label
Historically marketed as 'Rivanol', a classic yellow wound antiseptic
Extra-amniotic ethacridine instillation is a long-established, low-cost method of second-trimester abortion in many countries, often augmented with oxytocin and/or prostaglandins
Solution and patient secretions stain yellow - reassure patients this is expected
Modern medical abortion with mifepristone/misoprostol has largely replaced ethacridine instillation where available
missed: Ethacridine is given as a single procedure (intrauterine instillation) or applied topically as needed, not on a fixed daily oral schedule, so the concept of a missed dose does not apply. For induced abortion, a repeat instillation is performed by the clinician if expulsion has not occurred within the expected interval.
overdose: Systemic toxicity from topical use is rare given minimal absorption. Excessive systemic exposure could cause methemoglobinemia and local tissue toxicity. For abortifacient use, complications relate to the procedure (hemorrhage, infection, incomplete abortion). Management is supportive and procedure-specific: treat methemoglobinemia with methylene blue if significant, and manage obstetric complications with evacuation, antibiotics, and resuscitation as needed.
